Commentary.Commentary: The umpires and the players are back on the field. Kraigg Brathwaite and Tagenarine Chanderpaul will open the innings for West Indies. Victor Nyauchi has been given the new ball and will begin proceedings. Let's play...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Right then, Zimbabwe took a brave decision here. West Indies will come out to bat with a 68-run lead. It will be interesting to see their approach and how they manage the to get through the Day's play. Zimbabwe have an opportunity to put the visitors under pressure by taking a few wickets before Stumps. Will either team be able to make a game out of this match? We will find out as West Indies come out to bat for the second time.

West Indies will be disappointed with their bowling effort here. They struggled a bit at the start but finished Day 3 on top with three wickets and started Day 4 in the same fashion picking up four wickets in the first session. They were in pole position to force the follow-on. However it went downhill after that as they had now answers to the Ballance-Mavuta partnership in the second session. They were able to break that stand after a lot of work, but then the tail-enders also added some crucial runs for Zimbabwe. Alzarri Joseph was the pick of the bowlers with three wickets while Gudakesh Motie and Jason Holder got a couple each. Kemar Roach and Kraigg Brathwaite also got into the wickets column.

Zimbabwe have done exceptionally well with the blade here. They still trail by, but they had to work hard to reach this point. The star of the show for them was the debutant, Gary Ballance who scored a special century to give his team a chance to save this game. At the start of their innings Innocent Kaia and Tanunurwa Makoni built up a good partnership of 63 runs, but then they lost their way a little bit. However, Kaia racked up his fifty and kept hold of one end while losing partners at the other. He too was dismissed and the middle order could not contribute that much. The fightback was led by Ballance who was well supported by Brandon Mavuta who himself got to his maiden Test half-century. Both of them added 135-runs for the seventh wicket. This not only saved the follow-on, but took the hosts well past that score and reduced the lead massively. Some quick-fire runs from Victor Nyauchi and Richard Ngarava also helped them. They will try to now restrict the Windies batter to not extend the lead hugely that could put pressure on them when they come out to bat again.

Hang on! Zimbabwe have declared their innings here! This may come as a surprise to many, but it looks like a good decision from Craig Ervine. They still trail by 68 runs and now they will look to get through West Indies batting line-up quickly. This is surely a brave decision from them and shows that they believe in themseleves.

Going into this session, the visitors has their tails up as they needed just three wickets to make their opponents bat again in their quest for a win. Their bowling attack was completely blunted by the batters and they also have themselves to blame for the situation of this game. Jason Holder dropped an absolute sitter when Brandon Mavuta just arrived at the crease and it seemed to cost them massively. They lost their discipline as the deficit began to reduce and they allowed the batters to score freely with the new ball not being effective as well. Will they be able to wrap up the innings soon? Or will Zimbabwe continue to rack up the runs? We will find out shortly when we return for the final session of Day 4 at 6.30 pm IST (1 pm GMT).

A massive smile on the faces of the Zimbabwe players! This has been a remarkable session for the hosts as they have given themselves a good chance of drawing this game by avoiding the follow-on. Gary Ballance has been the hero for Zimbabwe as he notched up a Test century on his debut for this nation and helped drag his team out of deep trouble. He was ably supported by Brandon Mavuta who initially struggled at the wicket but gained confidence and scored his maiden Test half-century. They have put together an unbeaten 121-run partnership in 201 deliveries and they now trail the West Indies by 134 runs making this now their game to lose with just one day left in the match.

Drinks! This has been a remarkable fight back from Zimbabwe as they have managed to not lose a single wicket in this session so far. They are now just 8 runs away from avoiding a follow-on and will be glad that they can get the West Indies to bat again. The visitors seem to have been ineffective in this second session as the new ball has also not provided much help. They are still ahead in this game but you can see the shoulders drop with the lack of wickets. A crucial period of play awaits us before the Tea break.

We are back for the second session of Day 4 and the umpires are out in the middle. West Indies have the advantage in this game as they make their way onto the field and take their respective fielding positions. Brandon Mavuta joins Gary Ballance out at the crease and they will need to build another good partnership to get Zimbabwe beyond the follow-on. Gudakesh Motie has the ball in hand and will finish his over. Let's go...
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

West Indies came out with a plan and they executed it very well. Alzarri Joseph looked lethal with his spell of bowling and provided two early breakthroughs. Kemar Roach then followed it up with another wicket. Their pacers continued to put the pressure on the batters, but could not get any more rewards. Gudakesh Motie too troubled the batters a bit with his off-breaks at the fag end of the session. and finally got his reward just before the end of the session which shifts the momentum again towards the Windies. Now, they will look to quickly get rid of the tail of Zimbabwe and make their grip more stronger in this match. Join us for the second session to catch all the exciting action at 4.10 pm IST (10.40 am GMT).

Lunch Break! A disastrous end for Zimbabwe in this session! They were looking good with the seventh wicket partnership between Gary Ballance and Wellington Masakadza, but the latter lost his patience just before the Lunch break and threw his wicket away. The hosts got off to a shaky start at the beginning of the session as they lost Innocent Kaia quite early. Tafadzwa Tsiga and Brad Evans followed suit. However, Gary Ballance used all his experience to recover the situation alongside Wellington Masakadza with a 55-runs stand, but now the whole responsibilty will be on Ballance to take Zimbabwe past the follow-on total.

OUT! CAUGHT! West Indies finally have a breakthrough and Zimbabwe lose their seventh wicket just on the brink of the Lunch! Wellington Masakadza seems to have lost his cool here as he plays a rash shot to undo all the good work they did over the last hour. Gudakesh Motie flights this one full and outside the off stump. Wellington Masakadza looks to drive it into the off side but is early into the shot as the ball seems to have held up slightly on the pitch. He lobs the ball to the left of mid off where Kyle Mayers moves quickly and grabs onto the catch. Zimbabwe will need to rebuild once again and West Indies will be hoping that they can take the last three wickets quickly to enforce the follow-on. That will be Lunch on Day 4!

We are all set for the game Day 4 to begin as the umpires make their way out to the middle. The West Indies players get onto the field and spread across to take their respective fielding positions. Innocent Kaia will continue his knock and is joined by Gary Ballance at the crease. Kraigg Brathwaite has the ball in his hand and will complete his over. Let's go...

Pitch Report - Darlington Matambanadzo is out at the center patch. He says that they had a full day's play and with the sun shining throughout it has dried the pitch up. Mentions that there are foot marks outside the off stump and a massive crack in the middle of the pitch. However, he reckons that it is still a good batting pitch as there is even pace and bounce so if the batters get it then can make the most of it.

Zimbabwe, on the other hand, could not be blamed that much, but their bowlers still needed to do a better job. The only positive for them was Brandon Mavuta, who picked up a five-fer which should give him a lot of confidence. However, after a good start to their batting innings, they lost their way a bit at the end. Now, it is up to the already half-centurion, Innocent Kaia, to hold one end and convert it into a big one, while Gary Ballance will try to use all his experience to get the host back in the game. This promises to be the Day where we get a clearer picture of the outcome of this game.

West Indies are on top at the moment thanks to a brilliant double hundred from Tagenarine Chanderpaul and a record-breaking opening partnership between him and Kraigg Brathwaite. This is a flat batting surface, and they took full advantage of that to put up a huge first-inning score. However, they were also able to take three wickets, the last being in the final over of Day 3, and they will be looking to pick up where they left off.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of Day 4 of the first Test match between Zimbabwe and West Indies. The first two days were a bit quiet and rain washed out a lot of overs too, but on Day 3 it picked up and we saw some exciting cricket and records being broken. We can expect that to continue and entertain us all.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1...

Right then, an engrossing day of Test cricket comes to a close where a few records tumbled and as many as 9 wickets fell. West Indies are easily ahead of the home team as they still lead by 333 runs. Day 4 looks to be the one where this game will firmly swing in one direction and with the forecast being clear for almost the whole day, it will be a good watch. Join us on Tuesday at 1 pm IST (7.30 am GMT) for all the action but our build-up as usual will begin a lot earlier. Cheers!

Innocent Kaia also comes up for a quick word. The Zimbabwean opener says that it's an amazing feeling to score his maiden Test fifty and he is still hungry to get a big one. Shares that the bowlers were bowling full and his plan was to play straight. Adds that the opening partnership was all about the basic stuff and he enjoyed his time in the middle.

Jason Holder comes up for a quick chat. Says that the boys really played well and praises the knocks of Kraigg Brathwaite and Tagenarine Chanderpaul. Adds that the opening stand not just laid the foundation for them but took it really deep. Feels that it's not easy to bat for the new batters. Mentions that everyone who has played the ball in the V has succeeded. Tells that they have to stay patient on this pitch and keep believing in their abilities.

Earlier, West Indies knew that the pitch was flat when they decided to declare on 447/6 and it showed as their experienced front-line pacers weren't able to trouble the Zimbabwe openers. Kemar Roach and Alzarri Joseph bowled good lines and lengths but were largely ineffective. Kyle Mayers and Gudakesh Motie operated at the start of the final session but it was when Joseph was brought back into the attack, things started to happen. He got rid of Makoni and Motie came back into the attack to get rid of Chamu Chibhabha as well. After that, there were a few half-chances created but West Indies failed to pick up a wicket. The breakthrough did come via a smart move by their skipper Kraigg Brathwaite who decided to bowl the final over of the day. The visitors will now look to make early inroads on Day 4 and press the advantage home.

Zimbabwe went into the final session at 21/0 in 10 overs and finished the day at 114/3 in 41.4 overs. They will be a touch disappointed with that effort in the end. The debutant openers, Innocent Kaia and Tanunurwa Makoni started steadily and were able to put away the bad balls. They put on a 63-run stand for the first wicket before Makoni was dismissed. Chamu Chibhabha came out with positive intent but was dismissed soon after and then it was the pair of Kaia and skipper Craig Ervine who looked to be doing extremely well until the very last over of the day in which the skipper was removed by his counterpart. Kaia though notched up a half century on debut and will be key for the hosts if they are to put up a fight with the bat on Day 4.

A dramatic end to the day's play and it is West Indies who will head into Day 4 with all the advantage they wanted thanks to that late wicket courtesy of their skipper. Day 3 is generally known as the moving day in Test cricket and the game surely moved at a brisk pace. The sun was out throughout the day and we were finally able to get a full day's worth of play.

OUT! BOWLED 'EM! Kraigg Brathwaite was at his best with the bowling changes and this one to bring himself into the attack has also earned his team a wicket. The West Indian players are running in celebration. Kraigg Brathwaite has removed his opposite number in the last over of the day's play. It will be Stumps on Day 3.
Slower through the air, full and on middle, Kaia lunges to defend and edges it wide of first slip. It speeds down to third man and they get a run.

Loopy and full, around off, Kaia drives it to covers.
Kraigg Brathwaite brings himself on to bowl the final over of the day.
Serves it full and on off, Ervine leans forward and offers a copybook defensive shot.

Quicker and fuller, on middle, defended back.

Too full and on off, driven back to the bowler.

Fuller and on off, defended off the front foot.

Slider around middle, Ervine defends it to the off side.
Shortish and on off, Ervine punches from the back foot but not in the gap. Straight to cover-point.

Floated delivery, full and on off, Kaia drives but finds mid off.
Short and on top of off, Kaia stands back and plays it towards point.
Goes back and turns it on the leg side, picks up a run.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Full and on off, driven to mid off.
A little too short and outside off, Ervine rocks back and whacks it past backward point. He picks up three runs. 100 comes up for Zimbabwe!
Leans forward to a full ball and taps it down defensively towards first slip.
Skidding in from around off, it's blocked off the back foot.
Flatter through the air, short and on off, Ervine punches it to mid off.
Shortish and close to off, Kaia plays late and dabs it down to backward point for a single.
Tossed up outside off, spinning in, Kaia goes on the back foot and defends it down.
Quicker and fuller, on middle, it's worked towards mid-wicket for one.
Turning down the leg side, Ervine nudges it behind square leg and picks up a single.
Skidding in from middle, Kaia defends it off the inner edge to square leg. They cross.
Loopy and full, around off, Kaia defends it off the front foot.
FOUR! Fine, fine shot! Quicker one, full and on off, Kaia goes down on one knee and sweeps it sweetly to the deep mid-wicket fence. Maiden fifty in Tests!

Beaten! Full and on off, angling away, Ervine tries to defend inside the line but misses.

On a length and around off, tapped down to point.

Pitches it up now on off stump, Makoni drives it gently toward mid off.
Good length in that channel around off and Makoni leaves it alone.

Not too far away! Short ball, attacking the rib cage and Innocent Kaia gets cramped for room. Kaia ends up jarring at it and defends it uppishly in front of the diving fielder at short square leg. They do get a single though.
Back of a length and around off, Kaia leaves it alone.
Maiden! Flights it up and bowls it around middle, Tanunurwa Makoni defends it off the front foot.
On middle and leg, this is pushed away to mid on.
Flatter one outside off, Makoni cuts it straight toward point.
This one is sliding into the leg stump, Makoni just nudges it leg side.
This is fired in fuller and on middle, Tanunurwa Makoni manages to get a bat on it.
Gives it a nice loop and bowls it on off stump, Makoni blocks it out.
Good length on the pads, this is flicked away to deep square leg for a single.

EDGED AND FOUR! Bowled back of a length outside off and leaving the batter. Tanunurwa Makoni doesn't move his feet and has a little nibble at the ball away from his body. The outside edge is found but luckily for him, the ball goes in between first slip and gully and into the fence.
Back of a length and angled in from outside off, Makoni stays back and pushes it out on the off side.
This is banged in even shorter but angling down leg. Tanunurwa Makoni ducks under it.
This is short and over middle, Innocent Kaia pulls it off the back foot to deep mid-wicket and picks up a run.
Slower one, on a length and around off, Kaia looks to flick but ends up playing all around it and gets hit high on the pads.
Pulls back the length now and bowls it outside off, Makoni plays it off the back foot toward point.
Flatter one on off stump, Makoni makes another block.
This is bowled on off stump, Makoni eases it onto the off side.
At the stumps, kept out by Makoni.
Shorter and on the pads, Innocent Kaia tucks it away through square leg and the fielder gives chase. The batters are able to get back for the third and bring up the 50-run stand as well.

A huge appeal for lbw and it does seem straight but the umpire says no. Gudakesh Motie slides this one onto middle and leg, Innocent Kaia looks to block but misses and gets pinged in front. There might have been an inside edge and that is what saved him.
Good length around middle, Makoni blocks it onto the deck.
FOUR! Gloriously driven! This is full and wide, Tanunurwa Makoni just leans on and creams it through the cover region for a lovely boundary.
Length again and on the pads, Kaia works it away behind square leg for a single.
Good length, angling into the off pole, Innocent Kaia solidly keeps it out.
This is full and just angling down leg, Kaia looks to flick but misses. The ball goes off the pads and rolls toward backward square leg.
Holder pitches it up around off stump, Kaia gets on the front foot and pushes it toward covers.
Short again, on off, Tanunurwa Makoni goes back to cut but finds the fielder at point.
Slightly short and on off, Makoni hangs back and defends it late to the off side.
Loopy and full, around off, defended safely off the front foot.
Pulls his length back and delivers it on off, Makoni goes on the back foot and blocks it to mid off.
Leans forward to a full ball and pushes it to covers.

NOT OUT! Flatter delivery, around leg, Makoni nudges it down to fine leg and returns for the second run. The throw comes to the keeper who collects the ball and breaks the stumps. They appeal. It's referred upstairs. The replays show that Makoni is safe. A direct hit would have got him.

An appeal for a run-out and the umpires have sent it upstairs. Tanunurwa Makoni was struggling a bit to get back to the keeper's end and the throw from deep backward square leg was a good one. The replays show that Makoni did make it in time.
Pitches it up and on off, Kaia lunges and defends it strongly.
Full and outside off, some extra bounce, Makoni tries to drive but it takes the outer portion of his bat. The ball finds the gap at cover-point and they cross.
Around middle and off, on a good length, Makoni stays back and defends it towards mid on again.
Fullish and on off, angling in, Makoni brings his bat down and defends it to mid on.
Delivers it ahead of a length outside off, Makoni drives but finds the fielder at mid off.
Slants a length ball on off, Makoni defends it from the back foot.
Leans forward to a full ball and blocks it to the off side.
Slower through the air, a touch short around off and turning away, Kaia defends it gently with an angled bat.
FOUR! Shot! Too full and around off, Kaia kneels down and sweeps it firmly in front of square on the leg side. It scoots away to the fence in no time.
Gets on the front foot and pushes a full ball to silly point.
Flighted and on middle, defended on the leg side.
Fuller around off, pushed towards mid on.
Bumper around middle and leg, Tanunurwa ducks easily.
On a length, around middle, it's defended off the back foot to square leg.
Holder perhaps loses the grip and slips a full toss down the leg side. Makoni fails to get any bat behind it.
Fuller and on off, Makoni brings his bat down and defends it to the leg side.
Around middle, on a length, Makoni works it off his pads but this time straight to mid-wicket.
Holder starts with a full ball around middle, Makoni flicks it in front of square on the leg side and picks up a couple of runs.
Jason Holder is now introduced into the attack.
Flatter through the air, around middle, Kaia goes on the back foot and defends it down safely.
Too full and around off, blocked to the off side.
Slower through the air, full and around off, Kaia presses forward and blocks it to covers.
A touch short and on off, Kaia gets close to the delivery and chops it down to short third man.
Full and floated, around off, defended to short cover.
Loopy and full, around middle, Kaia defends it off the inner edge to short mid-wicket.
Length around off, angling in, Makoni stays back and defends it from the shoulder of his bat.
Shortish and outside off, skidding off the surface, Makoni withdraws his bat at the last moment.
Back of a length on off, cutting back in, Makoni goes on the back foot and defends it in front of the fielder at silly mid on.
Angling in around middle, it's defended towards silly mid on.
FOUR! Classy shot! Full in length and outside off, Tanunurwa Makoni leans into the drive and thumps it through the gap at covers for a lovely boundary.

Muted appeal for a caught behind! Mayers delivers a length ball on middle and leg, drifting down, Makoni tries to flick but then withdraws the bat. The keeper collects it with a dive to his left and the slip cordon appeals. Nothing from the bowler.
Tossed up, around off and fuller in length, Kaia gets forward and defends again to end the over.
Fuller and on middle, defended back.

Huge shout for an lbw! Nothing from the umpire. Flighted and around off, turning away, Innocent offers no shot and pads it away. The impact is outside off but that's not the issue. That said, it's spinning away and would have missed the stumps. Easy decision for the umpire.
Pushes it quicker through the air, full and on off, Kaia draws forward and defends it to silly point.
Too full and around leg, Kaia drives down the ground but straight to mid on.
Fuller and on middle, skidding in, Kaia lunges and defends it off the inner edge.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it to short mid-wicket.
Mayers gets a length ball to shape back into the right-hander, Makoni stays back to cover the movement and pushes it softly to mid on.
Serves it on a length, close to off, Makoni stays back and pushes it to short cover.
Movement in the air. Full and curling in around off, Makoni helps it off his pads to mid-wicket.
Darts a length ball on off, Makoni covers the line and blocks it towards mid on.
On a good length and outside off, Makoni has a lazy push at it and it comes off the bottom part of his bat.
FOUR! Well played! Motie goes short and outside off, Kaia immediately goes on the back foot and cuts it firmly past backward point for a boundary.
Lands it full and on off, again Kaia draws forward and pushes it to short cover.
Fuller and on off, Kaia is forward in defense.
A friendly full toss, around off, Innocent Kaia doesn't pick that up and just defends it to the off side.
Very full and around middle, it's pushed down to mid on.
Floated delivery, full and on off, Kaia leans forward and defends it down.
Gudakesh Motie (1-1-0-0) to continue operating from the other end after the Tea break.
Presses forward to a full ball and pushes it gently to covers.
Angles in a full ball on off, Tanunurwa Makoni drives it back to the bowler this time.
Gets on the front foot and drives a full ball to covers.
The line is a bit too straight and the length is on the fuller side, Kaia nudges it down to long leg and rotates the strike.
This time it's full and around off, angling in, Innocent Kaia defends it back with a loose bottom hand.
A good start for the hosts! Mayers serves it on a length and outside off, Makoni opens the face of his bat and steers it wide of backward point. The fielder chases it down and they get three runs.

We are back for the final session on Day 3 and there are 32 overs remaining in the day's play. The two umpires are back in the middle and so are the players of West Indies. The openers for Zimbabwe, Innocent Kaia and Tanunurwa Makoni are all set to resume their stay on the crease. It will be Kyle Mayers to start proceedings with the ball here and he just bowled the solo maiden pover before the interval. Let's go...
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

In a short session with the bat, the Zimbabwean openers did well to absorb all the pressure. Both the Test debutants, Innocent Kaia and Tanunurwa Makoni, looked in control and didn't shy away from playing their shots. The pitch is not offering much to the pacers and the ball is coming nicely onto the bat. That said, the West Indian seamers have extra pace and bounce and they can cause issues. It remains to be seen how much support Gudakesh Motie will extract from this pitch. Just one over from him so far and it's not enough to pass the verdict. We can expect to see more of him in the final session which will get underway at 6.30 pm IST (1 pm GMT).
Too full and on middle, Kaia eases it down to mid on. That will be Tea on Day 3.
Flatter and a touch shorter on middle, Kaia helps it a bit aerially towards mid-wicket.
Flighted and full, around off, Kaia defends it off the front foot.
Very full again, in fact a low full toss, and Innocent Kaia just eases it back to the bowler.
Floated up full and on off stump, Kaia solidly blocks it out.

NOT OUT! Gudakesh Motie tosses it up first up and bowls it really full on middle. Innocent Kaia gets on the front foot and looks to block but hits the ball straight to the man at silly point. The fielder there pouches the ball and there is a loud appeal from Joshua Da Silva behind the stumps for a catch. It is checked by the third umpire and clearly, the ball had bounced before going to the fielder.
Appeal for a catch. Is it a bump ball? The two umpires get together and then refer it upstairs. The soft signal is not out. It will stay as not out. The replays confirm that it's bounced.
Gudakesh Motie to bowl the last over before Tea.
A maiden to start with! This is full and outside off, on the fifth stump line. Makoni leaves it alone.
This is pitched up around off, and Makoni punches it firmly to the man at covers.
On a length and pushed well wide of the off stump, Tanunurwa Makoni goes after it but fails to connect.
Keeps the length fuller and bowls it around off, Tanunurwa Makoni pushes it toward mid off.
Right in the blockhole around off and swinging back in a long way. Makoni looks to jam it out but fails to do so.
Kyle Mayers comes into the attack now and starts off with a fullish delivery. This one angles in from around off and Makoni firmly pushes it to mid off.
A bouncer now, over middle, and Kaia just ducks under the ball.
Pacy delivery, on a hard length and jagging back in sharply. Innocent Kaia looks to block but gets beaten by the pace and gets hit on the thigh pad.
Fullish length around off stump and Kaia keeps it out on the off side.
FOUR! Overpitched and punsihed! This is a half-volley outside off, Innocent Kaia just leans on and creams it through extra cover for a boundary.
Short and wide, slapped away off the back foot with good timing but straight to the man at backward point. Gudakesh Motie there fumbles a bit and they are able to get a single.
FOUR! Nicely done! This is on a length and on middle and leg, Tanunurwa Makoni just punches it on the up and the ball just rolls away into the vacant long on fence. Lovely timing from Makoni!
Back of a length and on the pads, Tanunurwa Makoni tucks it away to the right of deep square leg and gets off the mark in Test cricket with a single. They should have got two though.
Shortish length over middle, Makoni dabs it down towards mid-wicket.
Short of a length and angling back in from outside off, Makoni looks to drive but mistimes it onto the leg side.
On a good length and angling into middle, Tanunurwa Makoni looks to block but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Hard length outside off, Kaia tentatively pushes the ball in front of point and gets across for an easy single.
This is pitched up around off and angling in, Innocent Kaia drives it on the up to mid off.
A length ball now on the fourth stump line and Makoni makes a watchful leave.
Hard length around middle and this one nips back in sharply. Makoni looks to tuck it away but gets hit on the body.
A quick bumper now at the body, Innocent Kaia gets rushed a bit but does well to get inside the line. He plays a reactive pull shot down to fine leg for a single.
Back of a length and outside off, Kaia looks to punch off the back foot but the ball stays low and beats the under edge.
Keeps it fuller and brings the ball close to the off stump, Innocent Kaia plays at it with soft hands and edges it down past the gully fielder for a couple of runs.
On a fullish length and on the fifth stump line, Kaia shoulders arms at it.
Goes fuller now and tries to angle it into the off stump, Tanunurwa Makoni blocks it off the front foot.
Short this time and over middle, Kaia pulls it a bit aerially and toward deep square leg for a single.
On a hard length around off and just shaping away, Kaia leaves it alone for the keeper to collect.
Extra bounce! Good length again, trying to swing it away from the middle and leg line. Kaia looks to block but gets a bit taken aback by the bounce.
A fraction shorter and on the pads, Innocent Kaia works it off his hips down to deep square leg for a couple of runs.
Good length, angling down the leg side and left alone by Innocent Kaia.
Maiden! Back of a length and on the body, Makoni keeps it down in front of short leg.
A quick bumper now over the stumps and Makoni ducks under it well.

Was there a glove on it? Doesn't look like it and the umpire says no as well. Alzarri Joseph digs it in short and at the body, Tanunurwa Makoni tries to get out of the way but the ball goes off his body and pops up around short leg. The fielder there pouches the ball and there's a stifled appeal but nothing doing.
Just a bit shorter and around off, Makoni leaves it alone.
Beaten! Keeps the length good and keeps the line tight around off stump. Tanunurwa Makoni looks to drive it through covers but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Good length, in the channel around off and Tanunurwa Makoni shoulders arms.
Goes fuller and tries to attack the stumps, the ball skids on as well but Kaia manages to push it toward mid on. A maiden!
Roach goes a bit wide of the crease and angles in a fullish delivery from outside off. Kaia solidly blocks it out.
Good length around the top of middle, Kaia blocks it off the front foot.
This is full again and angling into middle and leg, Innocent Kaia gets on the front foot and drives it straight to mid on.
This is pitched up around off, Innocent Kaia punches it straight back to the bowler.
The batter has just watchfully blocked this out.
Aggressive bowling this from Alzarri Joseph. Bangs in a pacy bouncer over middle and leg but Tanunurwa Makoni does well to bend his back and get out of the way of the delivery.
On a good length around middle and leg, Makoni nudges it onto the leg side.
Nicely bowled! Good length in that channel around off and just holding its line. Tanunurwa Makoni plays inside the line of the ball and the ball zips past the outside edge.
Loose delivery and a loose shot as well from the debutant. This is short and wide, there to be hit and Tanunurwa Makoni looks to slap it away but misses.
Pacy delivery, short of a length and around off, Tanunurwa Makoni shoulders arms at it.
Joseph starts off with a shortish delivery that is angled at the body. Innocent Kaia tucks it away toward mid-wicket and scampers through to the other end.
Alzarri Joseph to share the new ball from the opposite end. Three slips and a gully waiting...
Full and on the pads, this is clipped away to deep backward square leg for one. Three runs come off the first over for Zimbabwe.
Good looking shot for no run. This is pitched up on off stump, Innocent Kaia drives it firmly but finds the man at mid off.
Fuller and angling into middle and leg, Innocent Kaia works it away through square leg for a couple of runs and opens his account in Test cricket. Zimbabwe are also underway!
Good length again around middle, Innocent Kaia punches it straight to mid on.
Roach looks to go a bit fuller and attack the pads but spills it down the leg side, Innocent Kaia leaves it alone for the keeper to collect.
Starts off with a good-length delivery, angling into middle. Innocent Kaia gets a good stride forward and pushes it toward mid on.
